verbalization: Sinuflexibilin appears to interact with Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1 through a series of molecular targets, with Lactase-phlorizin hydrolase acting as a central mediator. This enzyme is targeted by both Jasminoside T and Beta-D-Glucopyranosyl-(Z)-3-Hexenol, which in turn are predicted to interact with the transporter. The integration of these pathways suggests that Sinuflexibilin may modulate the activity of this transporter via its interaction with these compounds, potentially influencing anion transport in cellular processes. The evidence supports a mechanism where Sinuflexibilin indirectly affects the transporter through its targets, highlighting a complex network of interactions that may underlie the drug's biological effects. The relationship is further supported by the consistent presence of Lactase-phlorizin hydrolase as a common target, reinforcing the notion of a shared functional role in the transport process.
